title: Shadowy figures have been seen at a Penarth pub named one of the UK's most haunted
excerpt: Penarth's Captain's Wife has been named among the UK's most haunted pubs, with tales of smugglers, restless spirits and ghost sightings ahead of Hallowe'en.
content:
A pint with a side of the paranormal could be on the menu for your next night out.

The Captain’s Wife in Penarth has been named one of the UK’s most haunted pubs by Eat Drink Meet, a website that helps users discover nearby pubs, bars, and restaurants.

The list highlights 13 pubs, because no other number is fitting, with chilling histories of ghostly activity and unexplained sightings, offering a spooky twist for those looking to add a little fright to their next pub experience.

The Captain’s Wife, once known as Sully House thanks to nearby Sully Island, overlooks the Bristol Channel and is believed to be haunted by several restless spirits.

There are multiple tales of ghostly apparitions (Image: Supplied)

The pub’s eerie atmosphere is partly attributed to its history of smuggling and piracy along the Welsh coastline, which has inspired many of the ghost stories told by staff and visitors alike.

Among the pub’s most well-known spirits is Mrs Rhys, who is said to have drowned after running away to sea with her young lover.

Another tale tells of the pub’s namesake, whose wife’s body was reportedly stored in a box in nearby woods.

The box was mistaken for treasure and stolen by thieves and her spirit is now said to appear as a dark shadow, according to eyewitnesses.

A third mysterious female apparition is said to walk through the bar doors and along the length of the lounge before vanishing into the fruit machine.

The pub is believed to be haunted by several restless spirits (Image: Supplied)

The ghost of a man in his 40s, described as having windswept hair, has also been spotted wandering the pub forlornly. 

Visitors have reported hearing the cries of a young child in the upstairs rooms, while another child’s ghost has been seen near the chimney in the bar area.

This child is believed to have died while trying to escape from his violent father.

As the autumn nights draw on and Hallowe'en creeps ever closer, this may prove to be the perfect spot for paranormal enthusiasts to kick back and relax, all while keeping an eye out for one of the pub's many ghostly inhabitants. 

The Captain's Wife finds itself in good company on this list, with other infamous pubs including The Castle in the Peak District, The Volunteer on Baker Street, and The Old White Swan in York - all incredibly prolific locations for 'ghost hunters' and investigators alike.
